title: AgentIdentityResolution
description: Agent identity resolution on POST /api/v1/sessions (TraigentSchema#616). The canonical identity of an agent is the Backend-minted, project-scoped agent id; what a client DECLARES (agent_key, agent_id, function_name) is a resolution input, never the identity. The resolved id is returned in the 201 body at `metadata.agent_id` (null for a JWT caller, who gets no session-agent binding; the top-level `agent_id` of the 201 schema is not populated by the Backend today). Before any write the Backend resolves the agent in this order: (1) the exact legacy lookup by `agent_key` or by the name derived from `function_name`: a hit is reused, unless both the request and that agent carry a code locator and the two differ, which is `agent_identity_conflict` (nothing created) when no agent matches the request's own locator; (2) only when no `agent_key` was sent and step 1 found nothing, the code locator: module + qualname read from `metadata.function_module` and either `metadata.function_qualname` (exact) or the flattened qualname recovered from `metadata.function_name` (NOT the top-level `function_name`). Exactly one match is reused, none creates a new agent, several is `agent_identity_ambiguous` and nothing is created. `metadata.function_relative_path` is read as a hint and is never compared by the Backend. Renaming or moving an unnamed function changes module or qualname and so resolves to a new agent. `agent_ref` is accepted by the request schema but RESERVED: the Backend does not yet use it for resolution. Display names, objectives, knobs and the run or privacy mode are never identity. Every request-side field is optional and additive, and the constraints on the locator fields apply only to a content-less request (`capabilities` contains `content_less_v1`); a user-chosen agent name is customer content (GNFR-PRIV-003) and a content-less request must not carry it, while code identifiers (module, qualname, repo-relative path) are not content.

CodeModule.description: Dotted Python module name of the decorated function (`function_module`). A code identifier, not content. Half of the code locator; compared exactly.

CodeQualname.description: Exact, unflattened `__qualname__` of the decorated function (`function_qualname`), for example `Router.route` or `build.<locals>.agent`. Optional refinement of the locator: the legacy `function_name` identifier flattens every `.` of the qualname to `_`, so `A.b_c` and `A_b.c` of one module send the same identifier. When BOTH the request and a stored agent carry an exact qualname they must be equal; when either side lacks one the flattened comparison stands.

CodeRelativePath.description: Repo-relative file path of the decorated function (`function_relative_path`), forward slashes. A code identifier, not content. A HINT only: the Backend reads it but never compares it, so moving a file does not change the resolved agent.

AgentIdentityAmbiguousResponse.description: 409 on POST /api/v1/sessions. More than one existing agent of the project matches the request's code locator. NOTHING was created (no agent, run, study or binding); retry with an explicit selector or after the duplicates are resolved. Fixed text; no request value is echoed. `details.candidate_agent_ids` is returned only to a caller authorized for every listed agent (API key: per-agent write access; JWT user: project editor plus the same per-agent check); any other caller receives the ordinary authorization denial, which carries no candidates.

message.const: More than one existing agent in this project matches this function. No agent was created; resolve the duplicates and retry.

error.const: More than one existing agent in this project matches this function. No agent was created; resolve the duplicates and retry.

candidate_agent_ids.description: Server-issued ids of the agents that match, in no order of preference (the Backend never picks a survivor).

AgentIdentityConflictResponse.description: 409 on POST /api/v1/sessions. The request's name (legacy `function_name` identity) matches an existing agent whose stored code locator is a DIFFERENT function, and no agent matches the request's own locator. The name match is never reused and nothing was created. Fixed text; no request value is echoed. `details.conflicting_agent_id` is returned only to a caller authorized for that agent (same rule as the ambiguous refusal).

message.const: An existing agent already uses this identity for a different function. No agent was created.

error.const: An existing agent already uses this identity for a different function. No agent was created.

CapabilityNotSupportedResponse.description: 400 on POST /api/v1/sessions. The request declares a capability this server does not support (today only `content_less_v1`, which the server does not yet answer in the create response; any other capability value is a schema violation, not this refusal). Raised BEFORE any write, so a client fails closed without leaving an agent, run or study behind. Fixed text; the offending value is never echoed and no `details` member is sent. A client that wants to fail even earlier can omit the capability and read the server's advertised `capabilities` from a previous create response.

message.const: A requested capability is not supported by this server; no session was created

error.const: A requested capability is not supported by this server; no session was created

AgentId.description: Backend-minted agent id (agents.id, UUID4). KNOWN GAP: the Backend can also hold agents whose id a caller supplied at creation (a legacy route accepts `id` / `agent_id`, up to 512 characters), and those ids are customer-chosen content, not opaque. The content-class ratchet admits no new `legacy_content` and no content-free class fits an arbitrary string, so this schema validates UUIDs only. Backend follow-up: disclose in an ambiguous or conflict refusal only ids that are UUIDs (or issue agent_ref values), and say nothing about the others.

DuplicateAgentCandidatesReport.description: Response of the read-only 'possible duplicate agents' report for one project. NOT YET SERVED: the Backend implements the report as a service function only and exposes no route, so no path in optimization_endpoints.json references this shape yet. It lists candidate groups and never merges, relinks, reparents, rewrites a key or picks a survivor. Names, keys and descriptions are customer content and are never returned: only server-issued ids, timestamps and counts.

project_id.description: Server-issued id of the project the report covers: a UUID, or the default project's `project_<32 hex>` id.

enum: The relative file path is a hint and is not compared.
Residual race window: when no agent existed at check time, creation re-resolves under a PostgreSQL advisory lock; on SQLite there is no lock.

DuplicateAgentGroup.description: One group of agents that may be the same logical agent. `same_module_and_qualname` groups carry `locator_precision` (`exact`: every member has an exact qualname; `flattened`: none has; `mixed`: exact members plus flattened-only members that would resolve to them) and `uncertainty` low for exact, medium otherwise. `shared_hash_suffix_only` groups (older rows with no stored locator that share the `(hash)` suffix of their display name) carry no `locator_precision` and `uncertainty` high: a lead, never a match. `decisive` is always false: whether the members are one agent is the owner's call.

run_count.description: Number of experiments (runs) filed under this agent, in the same tenant, project and owner scope as the report.
